        The Buffalo Bills will honor another key member of their iconic 1990s team. The franchise announced on Thursday night that it will retire Hall of Fame receiver Andre Reed's No. 83 during the 2027 season. Reed, who starred in Buffalo from 1985-99, is the franchise's all-time career leader with 941 catches, 13,095 yards and 86 touchdowns. He had an additional 85 catches for 1,229 yards and nine touchdowns in 17 playoff games. Reed has joined former teammates Jim Kelly, Bruce Smith and Thurman Thomas as the fourth Bills player in the organization's history to have his jersey number retired.  Kelly, Thomas and Bills owner Terry Pegula surprised Reed with the news. 
"Oh man, it's almost like the moment when we all got the call for him going into the Hall of Fame," Thomas said. "We knew that he deserved to be in the Hall of Fame, and it was kind of the same thing. One of the four guys that, when you mention the Bills, his name is always mentioned.
"You saw his work ethic when we were in training camp together for 12 years, like, yeah, that guy is special, and he was a big part of our run to try to win a Super Bowl here. There aren't too many people today that go over the middle as much as Andre Reed did back in the day. He took a lot of punishment, but he was always there for us."Reed was an integral part of Buffalo's historic run of success during the 1990s. While they didn't win a Super Bowl, Buffalo made history by becoming the first (and last) team to play in four consecutive Super Bowls. Reed caught eight passes for 153 yards in Buffalo's third of four consecutive trips to the big game. 
Buffalo's run also included the largest come-from-behind win in playoff history. The Bills overcame a 35-3 deficit to defeat the Oilers in the 1992 wild card round. Reed caught three consecutive touchdowns during Buffalo's comeback. 
Reed was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2014.

body:
The NFL threatened Nacua with potential "banishment" from the league for future violations of the personal conduct policy

    4:46 pm ET

            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL issued a three-game suspension to Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua on Thursday for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Nacua's suspension takes effect immediately, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, December 14, after the Rams' key divisional game against the San Francisco 49ers.Nacua is set to miss three high-stakes matchups against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and 49ers before he is eligible to return on December 20, in Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys.The NFL did not publicly disclose the nature of Nacua's personal conduct policy violation. It can be inferred, however, that the suspension is related to his ongoing civil suit, which stems from allegations that he bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark.The woman filed a temporary restraining order against Nacua in March. The lawsuit also mentioned allegations of gender violence and assault and battery. Nacua's attorney denied the allegations and said this is a "blackmail" attempt from the alleged victim on December 31, 2025.
According to ESPN, the NFL said it communicated to Nacua that "any further violation of the personal conduct policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the league."As unfortunate as the suspension is for Nacua, the timing is convenient. The Rams placed him on injured reserve on November 12 due to his PCL/MCL sprain and turf toe, so he was already set to miss at least four games during his recovery. Players may serve suspensions while on injured reserve, so he will complete the three-game ban during the remainder of his minimum IR stint. While suspended, Nacua will not be allowed in the team facilities, meaning he will not be allowed to rehab his injury with the team until the suspension is over. Previous instances of players serving suspensions while on injured reserve include Daniel Ekuale (2025), Sam Williams (2024), Mike Woods (2023), and David Parry (2018).
Puka Nacua absence timelineWeek 10: Placed on IR, missed game vs. CardinalsWeek 11: Suspension begins, remains on IR, Rams on byeWeek 12: Suspension continues, remains on IR, will miss game vs. PackersWeek 13: Suspension continues, remains on IR, will miss game vs. ChiefsWeek 14: Suspension continues, remains on IR, will miss game at 49ersWeek 15: Suspension to be lifted, eligible for reinstatement from IR, can play game vs. CowboysNacua already missed two games this season due to a hip injury, and the Rams went 1-1 in his absence in Weeks 2 and 3 against the New York Giants and Denver Broncos. Davante Adams stepped up in a big way as the team's No. 1 receiver and racked up 332 yards in those contests. Adams remains in the midst of his recovery from a hamstring injury but could return for the Rams' battle with the Packers, which would put him back at the top of the receiving pecking order.When he is on the field, Nacua remains a top-flight wide receiver. He averages 102.1 yards per game this year, which is high enough to make him the NFL's all-time leader in receiving yards per game at 96.2 over his career.Nacua has been a massive piece of the Rams' offensive game plan and saw at least seven targets in each of his first seven games of the year. He amassed a whopping 24 targets in Week 5 against the Buffalo Bills, which were the most by any player in a single game since 2009.

title: LSU president instructs Will Wade to not play RJ Luis amid potential SEC threat to expel Tigers from league - CBS Sports
description: One of college sports' biggest sagas of 2026 hit a true boiling point on Thursday, and just like that, Luis' coll
body:
One of college sports' biggest sagas of 2026 hit a true boiling point on Thursday, and just like that, Luis' college career could be over (again)
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Less than 24 hours after maybe the most controversial in-game substitution in college basketball history, LSU has seemingly surrendered in its fight to play former St. John's star/Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics signee RJ Luis.LSU president Wade Rousse issued a one-sentence update on Luis' status on Thursday night, sending the following press release: "In my role as president of the LSU system, after further review, I have instructed LSU men's basketball coach Will Wade not to play RJ Luis."Luis came off the bench early in the first half of LSU's 79-67 win over UL Monroe on Wednesday, logging 15 minutes and scoring 11 points in addition to grabbing nine rebounds. It was his first college basketball action since the second round of the 2025 NCAA Tournament, when he played for St. John's; Luis was the 2024-25 Big East Player of the Year.On Tuesday, Rousse was singing a very different tune after putting out a statement that attempted to justify LSU's obligation to roster Luis following a preliminary injunction that was handed down in an East Baton Rouge Parish courtroom on Nov. 13. 
"LSU is committed to compliance with NCAA and SEC rules, but it is equally committed to obeying the orders of Louisiana's courts. LSU is a member that will act in accordance with that order," Rousse wrote.
That statement was released after the SEC, through its legal counsel, released this statement Monday: "The SEC will abide by the terms of the preliminary injunction while it remains in place and will not impose penalties or fines on LSU if it places Mr. Luis on its men's basketball roster."This melodrama has engulfed the SEC for weeks. At issue was Luis doubling back to play college basketball after declaring for the NBA in the spring of 2025, then signing a pair of two-way contracts with the Jazz and Celtics that summer, only to get hurt and play in three preseason games. Luis committed to LSU in May 2026 and was litigating his way back to college thanks to the local Louisiana judiciary system. His situation is markedly different from the flood of other fifth-year lawsuits because he spent more than a year away from NCAA competition. In late August, after Luis won an initial temporary restraining order, the SEC ratified a new penalty structure against schools that attempt to roster a former professional athlete who was previously enrolled as a college student. The sanctions include lengthy suspensions for the head coach and hefty fines for the school in violation.
When Wade put Luis into the game against lowly Louisiana Monroe on Wednesday, it sent a "reaction of disbelief" around the SEC, per one conference source, who added, "it's been whiplash."Said another league source: "Everybody was surprised by it. It went from surprise last night to: what's the response?"The frustration around the conference increased so much that there were talks of potentially boycotting LSU games from league members if Luis was still playing with the Tigers by the start of SEC play the first week of January. In fact, sources told CBS Sports that Rousse's decision to take action on Luis Thursday also stemmed from the looming and increasingly real threat for the SEC to kick LSU out of the conference. 
One high-ranking SEC source refuted that framing to CBS Sports, though, saying that the discussion never reached that stage.Regardless, the temperature on the saga hit a boiling point this week — and LSU quickly came to understand what could eventually be at stake. Commissioner Greg Sankey and Rousse spoke at length on Thursday, shortly before SEC presidents met virtually for a regularly scheduled meeting, the aforementioned source told CBS Sports. It was on that phone call that Sankey ultimately got Rousse to stand down.It would take a two-thirds vote of qualifying executive members to purge LSU from the conference, per the league's bylaws.
The expulsion issue was first brought to the fore when LSU sought to roster two former Ole Miss players who failed to make NFL teams over the summer. When Lane Kiffin and the football program eventually flinched the day before LSU's first football game, the belief around the SEC was that Wade would not go as far as Kiffin did.Turns out, he and LSU's president went even further, guided by favorable court rulings in Louisiana that paved the way for Luis to be eligible. "The SEC's decision to threaten a member with expulsion if it plays an eligible student-athlete is reprehensible and seriously harms a young person who was caught in the middle of a power struggle having nothing to do with him," attorney Elliot Abrams, who is one of Luis' lawyers, told CBS Sports.
On Wednesday, Georgia's attorney general sent a letter to Sankey — his second in less than three months — that nudged the SEC toward severe action against LSU, "including expulsion" if the school didn't alter its behaviors. And in Birmingham, Alabama, there remains an ongoing federal lawsuit between the SEC and LSU, which was molded out of the shrapnel from the football roster fiasco in August.If Luis' days at LSU are numbered, another lawsuit may well be coming on his behalf. The school has an NIL contract with Luis, with significant money attached. LSU might ultimately have to pay Luis millions for just 15 minutes of playing time."I hope this issue is dead, but we'll be prepared for anything," another high-ranking of SEC member said.
When it comes to LSU, anything and everything is seemingly always on the table. It's how the school found itself in this vortex of controversy to begin with. Now we await the inevitable next action, because even if Luis' time at LSU could be over, there's no chance this is the last update on the LSU vs. SEC cage match.

That means the driver at -150 is a decent favorite to win, and you'd have to risk $150 to win $100. The second driver is a contender but is unlikely to win in the eyes of oddsmakers, but you'd win $200 after risking $100 if he does indeed pull off the upset.When you can bet on motor sports oddsThe racing schedule varies across NASCAR, F1 and IndyCar but there are usually weekly races with occasional breaks. NASCAR has multiple series, so there's usually at least one race across the series every weekend. F1 has a set calendar for the year with some breaks in between, but there are junior Formula racing series that might be going on in some of the gaps on the main circuit.Typically, the actual race will take place on a Sunday. There will be practice on either Thursday or Friday, with a qualifying event to set up the grid on either Friday or Saturday depending on the race schedule. Qualifying usually takes place the day before the race. Bettors can wager on qualifying outcomes as well, and those results will shift the race odds.Biggest races for motor sports bettingArguably, the biggest sporting event in the racing world is the Indianapolis 500, which is traditionally held on Memorial Day weekend. That's the premier IndyCar event.NASCAR has several big races, with the Daytona 500, a Crown Jewel event, regarded as the richest race on the circuit. The Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte and the Brickyard 400 are also considered Crown Jewel events. Talladega Speedway is a widely known track thanks to the movie "Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby", but it is not a Crown Jewel event.Every F1 race has its unique twist. The tracks are different in each city, but Monaco is considered the biggest spectacle of the season. The race itself is somewhat mundane because there's little opportunity for drivers to pass each other. The British Grand Prix at Silverstone, the Italian Grand Prix at Monza and the Singapore Grand Prix are considered some marquee events on the F1 calendar. The Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is also a high-profile event as it is typically last on the calendar and could decide who wins the drivers championship and constructors championship. F1 has also added special events like Miami and Las Vegas.Types of bets and how motor sports betting works Like all sports betting markets, there are a variety of ways prospective bettors can wager on motor sports. Here's a look at some of them.Outright/To win oddsThis market is straightforward. Users are betting on which driver will win the event. There are also markets here for which team/constructor car will win the event, which will have multiple cars involved.Here are the odds to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix, taking place on November 21, 2026. Odds are courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook and are current as of November 19, 2026.Max Verstappen +150Andrea Kimi Antonelli +350George Russell +370Lando Norris +500Isack Hadjar +1600Placement/Top Finish oddsMotor sports betting offers users the ability to wager on drivers or teams having a certain placement or finishing within a certain range. For example, you can wager on drivers to place in the top 5 or top 10 of the event. You can do the same with teams/constructors.While it rarely occurs in racing, there's a possibility of multiple drivers tying for a position. In this case, there are  technically multiple winning bets. However, sportsbooks grade dead heats differently and the payouts can be different. If FanDuel declares a dead heat, half the stake is applied at the original odds and half the stake is lost. If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.Dual ForecastThis is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. Both drivers must finish in the correct order for this wager to be paid out as a win. For example, you can wager on Max Verstappen and Lando Norris to finish first and second, respectively in a Dual Forecast market in F1 betting. However, if Verstappen finishes second and Norris finishes first, your bet will lose even though you did correctly pick the top two drivers for the race.Each Way BettingThis is not as common in motor sports but can be applied to racing betting. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.Stage WinnerThis is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.Matchups/Head-to-HeadSportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.Group WinnerThis is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.Top Car Make DriverThis is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. It's more applicable here since there are only two drivers on each F1 constructor, while car brands can span several NASCAR teams.Team of Race WinnerThis is similar to Outright Winner for drivers but applies to teams and constructors.Qualifying BetsBettors can wager on who will take pole position and which cars will be on pole. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. There are also different circuits like the Cup Series, the Xfinity Series and Truck Series. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.IndyCarThe major marquee futures market for IndyCar is the Indianapolis 500. Other than that race, there are season-long championship odds for the circuit.Can you parlay wagers in motor sports betting?While parlaying is generally not advised, as you don't get appropriate odds from sportsbooks that correspond to the actual chance of your bet winning, you are able to parlay outcomes in motor sports betting. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.How to bet on motor sports live during a raceSportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sportsDriver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers. Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. For example, Max Verstappen won the Canadian Grand Prix three years in a row and was a contender after starting second behind George Russell in 2025. Russell has had mixed results in Montreal historically but wound up winning the race after winning qualifying to take pole position.Longshots obviously don't usually win races, so they are better served as an inclusion in placement markets. You can usually back drivers who have had success on certain tracks or who have routinely finished just outside of a certain position market to break through eventually.Occasionally, a caution flag comes out when there's a crash on the track, which makes racing conditions hazardous for everyone. When this happens, there will be a safety car deployed, and all drivers must line up behind the safety car until the wreck is managed. There are different rules for each association and sometimes the race organizer makes a call in the moment, but usually, the race cannot end on a caution flag. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. title: UCLA vs. Michigan: Five things to watch as Bruins fight to stay undefeated, Wolverines desperate for big win - CBS Sports
description: UCLA and Michigan are having very different seasons, but both have plenty to play for on Saturday
body:
UCLA and Michigan are having very different seasons, but both have plenty to play for on Saturday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        No. 4 UCLA will travel to Ann Arbor on Saturday (3:30 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+ Premium) to face a Michigan team limping in after back-to-back losses. Both the Bruins and Wolverines are playing for first-year coaches, but it'd be hard for the vibes around Bob Chesney and Kyle Whittingham's inaugural seasons to feel more different.In Westwood, Chesney has become an instant legend for the turnaround he's authored with the Bruins. Yes, UCLA has had a fairly favorable schedule by avoiding Indiana and Ohio State, but a lesser team would be incapable of avoiding the pitfalls of the Big Ten schedule like UCLA has thus far to close in on their first-ever trip to the College Football Playoff. UCLA will have to resist the urge to look ahead to next week's battle with cross-town rival USC, but shouldn't find it too hard to be motivated to go into the Big House and get a win for the first time since 1982. 
Michigan is only three years removed from winning it all, but that 2023 national title feels like it was ages ago at this point in Ann Arbor. Whittingham was brought in to restore order for Michigan football, but at 5-5 with some truly awful losses -- most notably a 15-6 embarrassment against rival Michigan State -- there's growing chatter about Whittingham being a one-and-done. Bowl eligibility is far from guaranteed with a closing stretch featuring No. 4 UCLA and No. 14 Ohio State, and losses in the last two might seal Whittingham's fate as one of the worst Michigan hires in history. So, what should you be watching for as UCLA takes on Michigan on Saturday afternoon? These are the five things we'll be keying on. 
1. Who starts at QB for Michigan? Bryce Underwood underwhelmed to start the year and got benched at halftime against Penn State for Tommy Carr, who led a second-half comeback to beat the Nittany Lions. That represented the peak of Carr's tenure as the starter, as he likewise couldn't get the offense going, even after Michigan fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck. On Saturday, he was benched for Underwood. Kyle Whittingham said to start the week that it'd be a competition between the two in practice for the starting job on Saturday, and it's a sign of how bad things have been at the quarterback position that Michigan is having a competition in Week 12 of the season without having any injuries. Carr's stats are slightly better than Underwood's, but both have been dreadful against quality competition. Much of Carr's success came against Rutgers, while Underwood's best game was against UTEP. Against Big Ten defenses with a pulse, neither has consistently moved the football through the air, and Michigan has become painfully, predictably one-dimensional. 
Michigan has had an extra week to figure out something offensively that can present a challenge to the Bruins' defense, but given UCLA's been stingy on that end, Michigan will need to dig deep in the playbook to throw a real wrench in the Bruins' plans. 2. UCLA's shift to elite defenseThe Bruins began the season winning games in shootout fashion. Their games against Cal and Purdue in Weeks 1 and 3 were track meets, and it seemed like UCLA would be the kind of team that leaned on a high-powered offense to make up for a defense that had some holes. Then, almost overnight, the Bruins had it all click defensively and have been an elite unit ever since. Minnesota is the only team to reach 20 points on the Bruins since that 52-38 win over Purdue in Week 3, as the Bruins have stymied every opponent they've faced. While the schedule has presented them with some weaker offenses, that still includes Oregon on the road and an improved Illinois squad last week.
That has allowed UCLA to shift its identity with Ty Dieffenbach at quarterback. The rushing attack that was the best in the nation early on has cooled off considerably, and the Bruins have adjusted their offensive approach since losing Nico Iamaleava to injury. Now they focus on playing complementary football thanks to their defense making a midseason leap. Against Michigan, you can bet the game plan will be to find a way to get a lead and then make sure they force the Wolverines to prove they can drive the length of the field by avoiding turnovers and limiting mistakes. 3. The Dieffenbach-Mizell big play pairingUCLA is still committed to running the football, but after starting the year with 287 yards per game in the first three games, they've only topped 165 yards in a game once since. Defenses have loaded up to stop the run and dared Ty Dieffenbach to beat them over the top. 
The veteran backup has obliged, and while UCLA's offense isn't the sharpest or most efficient in the country, they are capable of a quick-strike score at any time. Dieffenbach has played in six games and is tied for sixth in the country with six passes of 50+ yards -- matching the likes of Drew Mestemaker, Noah Fifita and Gunner Stockton. All of those are to speedy receiver Aidan Mizell, who UCLA seems to be able to scheme open down the field about once a game. Dieffenbach rarely misses those opportunities, and those plays often make the difference in a UCLA win. The two hooked up twice for 75-yard touchdowns late against Minnesota to break that game open for a 14-point win, and while the Bruins lull defenses to sleep with their ground-and-pound attack, the entire time they're setting up opponents for the haymaker down the field. If Michigan's going to have a chance at the upset, they have to stay disciplined and prevent that big play over the top, because that's the exact type of play the Wolverines have struggled to make all year. 
4. Who makes plays without J.J. Buchanan?While UCLA knows exactly who its big-play threat is in the passing game, Michigan is now without its top receiver for the rest of the season. For a team that already struggled moving the ball through the air, losing Buchanan is a major blow for the Wolverines' offense. Buchanan accounted for 39.5% of Michigan's receiving yards this season (646) and 71.4% of their receiving touchdowns (5). He was the only reliable downfield threat and whether it was Underwood or Carr under center, he was about the only player who they would consider targeting over the top. Andrew Marsh leads the team in receptions (48) and figures to get an even greater target share without Buchanan, but much of his work is done in the short passing game. Given Michigan's struggles consistently moving the ball, creating big plays feels vital to their chances, but without Buchanan it's not obvious who they look to in order to create those. 
5. Does a win lock UCLA into the CFP? The Bruins can get to 11-0 with a win on Saturday that would also clinch a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game. With a ranked opponent left in No. 18 USC, one would think that would be enough to lock up their spot in the College Football Playoff's top 11. Given most of the teams on the outside looking in have three losses, it'd be an incredibly tough sell to boot UCLA for one of those teams; that said, this committee has been a bit unpredictable -- and has especially not been kind to the Big Ten. In years past, the committee has been adamant about not punishing teams for losing conference championship games, but there is at least some question as to whether the Bruins would be a lock if they ended up 11-2 with losses to USC and Indiana (their likely opponent in the Big Ten title game). A win on Saturday would seemingly put them into the bracket in pencil, but I don't think the Bruins will feel fully comfortable until they've got 12 wins (or the final rankings are out and they're officially in).

title: Texans vs. Colts prediction: Houston looks to bounce back on 'TNF' vs. lowly Indy after rough Week 10 loss - CBS Sports

Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup

        In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts.Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot.The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline.Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Follow the game live hereWhere to watch Texans vs. Colts liveDate: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ETLocation: NRG Stadium (Houston)Streaming: Amazon PrimeFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Colts have the ballThe Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces.Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL. Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions.
The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games.The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan, including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state.
When the Texans have the ballC.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season.The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner, either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins.It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. 
This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. PredictionI just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13

title: House GOP leaders plan December push for Protect College Sports Act - CBS Sports
description: Both the House and Senate must finish business before the new Congress is sworn in on Jan. 3, or the process star
body:
Both the House and Senate must finish business before the new Congress is sworn in on Jan. 3, or the process starts over in a Congress controlled by Democrats
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:02 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        College sports legislation that much of Washington had already buried is getting new life as lobbying efforts and negotiations over potential changes kicked into high gear this week.On Thursday, House Republican leaders gave the Protect College Sports Act something it hadn't yet had: a target date.House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, Education and Workforce Committee chairman Tim Walberg and Energy and Commerce Committee chairman Brett Guthrie said in a joint statement Thursday they plan to bring the landmark college sports bill to the House floor the first week of December, just in time for conference championship weekend."College sports are at a crossroad and Congress needs to pass strong antitrust protections to end the Wild West atmosphere that exists today," the three Republicans said. "We are committed to getting a bill to President Trump's desk that saves college sports."
The leadership also acknowledged the PCSA "in its current form faces real challenges in the House from many factions of our conference who take issue with several measures in the bill, along with Democrats outright opposing it.""We are working with our members to address as many issues as possible while keeping those changes narrow in order to maintain the fragile coalitions in the House and Senate," the statement said.Any change to the PCSA sends the bill back to the Senate, which passed it 77-22 on Sept. 28, and would require the chamber to vote on it again. The window is shrinking by the day, lending credence to the prospect that the bill will never pass. Both chambers must finish business before the new Congress is sworn in Jan. 3, or the process starts over in a Congress controlled by Democrats. The House's last scheduled day of work is Dec. 17, and government funding expires Dec. 11.
Texas Tech booster Cody Campbell and New York Yankees president Randy Levine, President Trump's strongest advocates for the bill outside Washington, D.C., spent Thursday on Capitol Hill. Sources tell CBS Sports that Big Ten commissioner Tony Pettiti is also lobbying heavily for the bill. Campbell, the Texas Tech board chairman whose Saving College Sports group is running a multimillion-dollar ad campaign during college football broadcasts, and Levine, the New York Yankees president and vice chair of President Trump's college sports roundtable, have led the outside push for the bill. A source close to Campbell said backers continue to believe the PCSA has broad enough support to pass the House and are encouraged by Scalise's commitment to a vote.Levine was blunter in a letter to House members last week. "History will remember if you choose wrong," he wrote. "Pass the PCSA."
Scalise has been among the most prominent Republican skeptics of the PCSA and a supporter of the SCORE Act, the House's own college sports bill, which leadership pulled from the floor three times earlier this year. He previously said the PCSA's neutrality on whether athletes can be employees would need to be addressed through amendments.But the objections run deeper than one provision in the 171-page bill, which would give schools, conferences and the NCAA targeted antitrust protection to enforce rules on athlete pay, eligibility and transfers, while also preempting patchwork state NIL laws and raising the revenue-sharing cap to $48.8 million per school.One of the biggest obstacles is a provision that caps power conferences at 20 members and restricts coaches from being hired away by other schools during the season.
Twenty-one House Republicans objected to that 20-member cap and to a three-year waiting period for schools that switch leagues in an Oct. 2 letter. Many hail from states with ACC schools that have actively sought exit plans from the conference.Florida Rep. Byron Donalds, the state's governor-elect, said last week: "I hate that bill."Others want an outright ban on classifying athletes as employees and a cap on international players. Walberg, one of three House leaders to announce their intention to push the bill forward Thursday, held a press conference Wednesday to discuss his own legislation, the TEAM USA Act, which would limit international players to 20 percent of varsity rosters.
The biggest obstacle might be the Democrats. The Congressional Black Caucus condemned the bill the day after the Senate vote, citing HBCU funding, the lack of employment rights for athletes and limits on their ability to sue. Democrats, who won control of both chambers in the Nov. 3 midterms, also have little incentive to hand the outgoing Republican majority a win. Republicans currently hold a 218-214 edge in the lame-duck House.Sen. Ted Cruz, the bill's lead Republican author, has been negotiating with House Democrats, Front Office Sports reported Wednesday. One idea on the table, either in the bill or as separate legislation, is a pathway to student loan forgiveness for HBCU attendees.Meanwhile, conferences are actively working on self-governance models to better police eligibility and athlete pay rules. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey said on the "Paul Finebaum Show" last week that "elections have consequences" and that the SEC is preparing for a future with or without the bill.
On Wednesday, the Knight Commission on Intercollegiate Athletics urged conferences to act on their own. It called on leagues to cap spending on coaching pay, buyouts, recruiting and facilities. They also asked to reserve a pool of conference revenue for schools that verify they follow the rules and to require every Division I school to disclose athlete compensation by sport. The commission said conferences should adopt its framework even if the PCSA passes."There is no excuse for inaction," Knight Commission co-chair Pam Bernard said.Time is running short on Capitol Hill, with only a two-week window and a de facto cram session facing House leadership aiming to bring the bill to the floor.

body:
A new player development rule, an executive leadership initiative and Austin as host of the 2027 Challenge Cup highlight the state of the league
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:53 pm ET

        The biggest week on the NWSL calendar is here as the buildup towards the 2026 NWSL Championship is underway. An awards show, countless events, and media days were all on the agenda ahead of Saturday's big game. That included the annual state of the league by commissioner Jessica Berman on Thursday. This year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m. ET. She also announced a few new league rules and future match events.  Here are the new things coming to NWSL:  NWSL player development rule The commissioner introduced the new player development rule. While the league previously submitted paperwork for a potential future second=division league, conversation and planning around that is currently paused with the upcoming 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup and efforts to grow NWSL in other ways. "As we grow from 16 to 18 teams in 2028, we know that we have to prioritize the pipeline, not just the pipeline of players, but the pipeline of talent that supports the players in the daily training environment. One of the things that makes the United States so uniquely positioned in the global women's soccer landscape is the depth of that potential pipeline," said Berman in her opening remarks. 
"That's why today we're announcing the NWSL Player Development Rule. It's an important step in strengthening the pathway to professional soccer for the next generation of players. The rule creates actual incentives for clubs to invest in identifying, developing, and retaining young talent, and it gives the clubs the flexibility to design their programs in the way that makes sense with their sporting philosophies." More information and the types of incentives will roll out for clubs as the new player development rule goes into effect, but it is another step in future roster-building for clubs now alongside general player signings, transfers, the High Impact Player rule, and the Under-18 mechanism. The addition of the rule is paving the way for more support staff and systems in place. The commissioner also announced the new NWSL Sporting Executive Program, meant to provide more support for club leadership development. The inaugural set of leadership includes six executives from the league who will participate in the program.  
"Developing the future of the sport is not just limited to the players; it's also about the technical staff who surround those players each and every day ... this is a first-of-its-kind program invested in talent, and it was curated and developed in collaboration with U.S. Soccer and FIFA. This new year-long initiative will provide sporting executives at our clubs with curated, specialized education, mentorship, and leadership development opportunities tailored around the unique demands of our league and the women's professional game," she said.  The 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup location The NWSL commissioner then announced the future site of the next NWSL Challenge Cup. The 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup will take place in Austin, Texas, next summer. The tournament has evolved since its first iteration as a placeholder for the COVID-19-affected season and is now a unique one-off marquee match between top clubs, typically the NWSL Shield titleholders and the NWSL Championship winners. In years where one club wins both, the game is a rematch of the previous NWSL Championship match. 
"Following the success of this year's Challenge Cup in Columbus, where we took the event to a neutral site to give an opportunity to introduce the NWSL to a new community," she said. The 2026 NWSL Challenge Cup was between 2025 NWSL Shield winners Kansas City Current and 2025 NWSL Championship winners Gotham FC. The 2026 competition was held in Columbus, Ohio. The state will now welcome its first NWSL franchise in 2028 alongside another expansion club in Atlanta.  Fans will undoubtedly make the connection and wonder if there is a future where an NWSL club calls Austin home. Currently, there are three NWSL clubs in California and only one in Texas, the Houston Dash.  
"We're really excited to create another special experience for our fans and our players while making the NWSL a place that can invite new audiences," Berman said about heading to Austin.  League evolution and expansion Commissioner Berman celebrated the league's recent return to the nation's capital for another NWSL Championship. The city hosted the 2022 event and now returns four years later with more attention on the league, the clubs, and its players than ever before.  "Today, we're bigger, stronger, more visible, and more ambitious than ever before, and the next five years are going to redefine what's possible. We have an extraordinary opportunity in front of us, and we intend to seize it," she said. 
Two incoming clubs set for 2028 and new player roster rules are just the beginning of NWSL's next chapter. There's still the potential for more clubs on the horizon, and current clubs Houston Dash and Racing Louisville are in the process of vetting for a sale to new ownership as franchise entry fees into the league are booming to new heights. And of course, there is still the biggest game of the year to play on Saturday. "The Washington Spirit are back in the championship for the third consecutive year, determined to bring home that title. And standing in their way is the Kansas City Current, with its own ambitions to win a championship after winning the Shield in 2025. These are two exceptional clubs, two incredibly passionate fan base, and the championship is still to be decided, [we're] very excited about the rest of this week."

Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds             Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.              The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                         Win             The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                          Place             The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.              Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                           Show             A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                           Win/Place             Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                           Place/Show             The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                           Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)              Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.              It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                           The most popular horse racing bet types             Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).              It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.               Exactas             An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.  Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                           Trifectas             This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.              The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                           Superfectas             Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                          Super High 5             Some books will allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in other forms of sports betting.  The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                          Box             A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.              For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:             $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:             $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.              A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                           How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers             While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                           Daily Double             The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.              Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                           Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6             Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.             Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.              The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.  For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                           Understanding horse racing payouts             After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.              The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:             2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								             $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								             				             $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				             If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.              For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:              2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				            Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting            The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.             January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes             Triple Crown of horse racing             The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.              Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.              The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                           Tips and advice for betting on horse racing             There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                           Racing forms and past performances             Racing forms are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                           Track conditions             Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                           Horse tendencies              From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.              The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                           Post position             Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                          Trainer and jockey information             A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                           Workout times             There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                           Speed figures             Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.              Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                          Manage your horse racing betting bankroll             Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                           Rules and responsible gaming             Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.             Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.               FAQ    How to bet on horse racing?  There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.    How to bet on horse racing online?  Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.    What is a box bet in horse racing?  A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.    What is a show bet in horse racing?  A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.    What is a key box bet in horse racing?  A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

        Two of college basketball's most storied brands will square off at 8 p.m. ET Friday at Lucas Oil Stadium when Kentucky tangles with Indiana on CBS. The Wildcats (4-1) will be seeking a much-needed course correction following a rocky start, but they will have to contend with a Hoosiers team that is 5-0 after knocking off Arkansas on Tuesday. title: Bengals duo could break NFL record that has stood for 31 years: Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on historic pace - CBS Sports
description: Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins could make NFL history for the red hot Bengals
body:
Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins could make NFL history for the red hot Bengals
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        CINCINNATI -- The Cincinnati Bengals offense has been nearly unstoppable this year. Heading into Week 11, Joe Burrow is the MVP favorite and one of the reasons that he's been so successful this year is because he has arguably the top receiving tandem in the league in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Through the first 10 weeks, there are only seven players in the NFL who have topped 800 receiving yards, and both Bengals players are on that list. Chase ranks fourth in the NFL with 878 receiving yards while Higgins is right behind him with 824 yards, which ranks sixth in the league. Chase and Higgins are just the fourth receiving duo in NFL history to both hit the 800-yard mark in just nine games (Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have also topped 800 yards this year, but the Packers duo has played 10 games compared to just nine for the Bengals duo). The two Cincinnati receivers are both on pace to finish with more than 1,500 yards, which is mostly notable because no team has ever had TWO players hit 1,500 yards in the same season. As a matter of fact, it's been 26 years since a duo even came close to hitting that mark. 
Back in 2000, Torry Holt finished with 1,635 yards while playing for the "Greatest Show on Turf" Rams and his teammate, Isaac Bruce, finished with 1,471. In 1995, the Lions' receiving tandem of Herman Moore (1,686) and Brent Perriman (1,488) came closer than anyone to having two players on the same team hit 1,500 yards, but Perriman came up 12 yards short. The Lions duo totaled 3,174 yards, which is the NFL record for a receiving tandem. The record has somehow stood for 31 years, even with the league now in a pass-happy era. This year, Chase is on pace for 1,658 yards while Higgins is on pace for 1,556, which would put them at 3,214, topping Moore and Perriman. During a press conference on Thursday, Chase was asked if it would be meaningful for him and Higgins to become the first duo to top 1,500 yards in the same season, and he didn't hesitate with his answer. "100%," Chase said. "I'm not pushing for it, but I'm definitely speaking it into existence with me and Tee." 
This week, the Bengals get to face a Commanders defense that has given up at least 120 receiving yards to five different players this season, so Chase and/or Higgins could end up having a big game on Monday night. Burrow is good at spreading the ball around, which is why Chase and Higgins are both succeeding. Both guys have been hot at different times this season. There was a four-game span starting in Week 4 where Higgins topped 145 yards in three of four games. As for Chase, he's been unstoppable over the Bengals' past three games, catching 32 passes for 527 yards. In terms of NFL history, Jerry Rice is the only player who's had a better three-game span and that happened back in 1995. 
One reason the Bengals' star duo is putting up such big numbers is that opposing defenses can't seem to figure out who they should take out of the game. "What all that going on with me and Tee is just how the coverage works out," Chase said of why one of them always seems to be open. "Maybe a coverage could be sliding to my side the whole time, but then the coverage that's sliding to my side is the look we want or maybe it's the opposite, they're going to my side and it's not open, but Tee's getting a one-on-one on the backside. It's really pick your poison playing with us. And this year, Tee's jumped into more of a bigger role of his play than usually."Chase and Higgins have both hit 1,000 yards in the same season twice, but that hasn't happened since 2022. Both guys could hit that number before the month of November is over, and if that happens, they'll have their sights set on the historic 1,500-yard mark that no duo has ever hit.
